problems.title: The final thread reads past packed gap storage
problems.source_location: Section 2.3.2; decode.cu, lines 85–87; encode packing function, lines 164–170
claim: Each of \(512B\) launched threads stores a \(5\)-bit gap. The decoder reads bytes \(q=\lfloor5i/8\rfloor\) and \(q+1\) without a sentinel or conditional.
analysis: The array has \(320B\) bytes. At \(i=512B-1\), \(5i=8(320B-1)+3\), so the second read is index \(320B\), one past storage. A valid example with \(2048\) one-bit and \(2048\) two-bit encoded exponents produces \(768\) compressed bytes and one block, hence reads \(319,320\) from \(320\) gap bytes. Alignment \(3\) shifts by \(8\), discarding the second byte, so its value cannot alter the extracted gap. Allocator padding may make it physically readable; no GPU crash or corrupted-weight result is established.
result: The logical-array contract fails on the final thread of every nonempty launch in this configuration. Accuracy and speed measurements remain unrefuted.
repair: For alignment \(r=5i\bmod8\le3\), extract from byte \(q\) alone by shifting \(3-r\) and masking \(31\); otherwise retain two-byte extraction. Every requested field is present, and the omitted low byte would have been discarded. CUDA integration/performance remains unverified.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The exact unnecessary read is local and its bits are discarded; central scientific damage is not established.

problems.title: Inactive-tail counting needs an initialization contract
problems.source_location: decode.cu, register_buffer declaration, conditional loads and first counting loop
claim: Threads conditionally load input bytes, but every launched thread copies those registers into its counting buffer.
analysis: For \(768\) bytes at \(8\) bytes per thread, only threads \(0\) through \(95\) receive input; \(416\) tail threads do not. Padded gaps do not initialize those registers. Bounded final writes and suffix counts can nevertheless leave earlier outputs intact. Actual reachable lookup values, loop progress and synchronization need a native GPU check; arbitrary assumed register values do not establish an observed symptom.
result: Missing initialization is a visible source obligation, but its runtime/output consequence and a complete repair remain unresolved.
problems.impact_rationale: Static missing initialization alone does not identify a CUDA failure or wrong model result.
